title: coord serve serves the committed policy and the group overrides as two OPA bundles that answer 304 when unchanged
goal: coord.py serve --policy-dir DIR answers GET /v1/bundles/kbjobs.tar.gz (DIR's .rego and data files, manifest roots kbjobs/placement and kbjobs/groups) and GET /v1/bundles/kbjobs-overrides.tar.gz (data.json under kbjobs/overrides, mapping each group path to its override, manifest root kbjobs/overrides), both behind the same bearer check as POST /v1/run, each with an ETag that changes only with its content and 304 for a matching If-None-Match; a missing --policy-dir answers 404 for the first bundle only

gates.question: Which files of --policy-dir does the kbjobs bundle carry, and how does serve treat other GET paths?
options: Every .rego plus data.json, data.yaml and data.yml, no hidden files or symlinks; any other GET path answers 404 after the bearer check
Every .rego plus data.json only; any other GET path answers 405
gates.recommendation: Every .rego plus data.json, data.yaml and data.yml, no hidden files or symlinks; any other GET path answers 404 after the bearer check
gates.answer: Every .rego plus data.json and data.yaml, no hidden files or symlinks, and no data.yml: OPA v1.21.3 parses only data.json and data.yaml as data (bundle.go IsStructuredDoc, kb public/agents/policy-as-code.md), so a data.yml would ship as a plain file and break the signing hash of ST-vxwngvv7; any other GET path answers 404 after the bearer check

gates.question: How is a bundle's ETag made, and is a value that is not a JSON object served in the overrides?
options: ETag is the SHA-256 of the bundle bytes, which carry fixed times and owners; a value that is not a JSON object is left out
ETag is the store's highest revision of the group keys; a value that is not a JSON object is served as it is
gates.recommendation: ETag is the SHA-256 of the bundle bytes, which carry fixed times and owners; a value that is not a JSON object is left out
gates.answer: ETag is the SHA-256 of the bundle bytes, which carry fixed times and owners; a value that is not a JSON object is left out
